subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: AGENDA 1 (intent vs oversight): The true default at plugin-init.ts:282 is an INCOMPLETE MIGRATION, not a deliberate fail-safe. ADR-0005:3/22/24, deployment-notes:10/21, and CHANGELOG:187 all record the deliberate intent to flip to false (commit bbbbdbca4); ADR-0005:24 explicitly classifies true as 'incorrect behavior under per-session routing'. The flip landed in the schema helper (types/project.ts:174-177), docs, and status projection (status.ts:678) but not at the one runtime call site that decides worker spawn. LIMITATION: no bash/shell tool was available in this read-only surface, so commit bbbbdbca4 was not introspected directly; the conclusion rests on the corroborating ADR + docs + live-source contradiction. AGENDA 2 (other call sites): worker_singleton_enforce is read ONLY at plugin-init.ts:279 — that is the sole behavioral divergence. worktree_guard_enforce is read via two DUPLICATE readBooleanFeatureFlag copies (worktree-auto-manage.ts:80, task.ts:194/271), all correctly defaulting true (matching the helper). So RC1 is not a multi-flag drift today, BUT there are 4 feature-flag resolvers (1 helper + 3 ad-hoc copies) instead of 1 owner — a latent footgun where any new flag default added to the helper silently won't reach the ad-hoc readers. AGENDA 3 (rq-workerSingleton01 currency): NOT stale. It describes singleton-lock coordination CONDITIONAL on enforcement being active; it mandates no default and is still correct law for projects that deliberately set enforce:true. The violated law is rq-advcfg01.2 (default false), which the runtime contradicts — fix the runtime, do not amend either spec beyond an optional clarifying note. RC2 (archive sync): confirmed unexecutable. syncDefaultBranchAfterMerge has zero production callers and no tool surface; adv-archive.md:517 treats command prose as an executable surface, which it is not. The git-finalize.test.ts:4538 boundary only forbids INTERNAL-within-git-finalize.ts callers, so an external caller (archive tool handler or new tool) is permitted. DESIGN-INDEPENDENT OBJECTIVES: O1 route the runtime worker_singleton resolution through withStabilityFeatureDefaults (one owner); O2 adv_status and runtime must share that one resolver; O3 RC2 needs an executable surface (tool OR fold-into-archive-handler) or explicit deletion+manual-doc; O4 RC2 sync is coupled to RC3 — MAIN_NOT_ON_DEFAULT (git-finalize.ts:217) blocks when trunk is dirty/on-wrong-branch, exactly the pokeedge/pokeedge-web trunk state, so trunk cleanup must precede or accompany RC2 for sync to ever succeed.

validation.notes: All three root-cause defects (RC1/RC2/RC3) confirmed by file:line + spec-law + ADR evidence with no contradictory evidence. No redesign blockers. Caution (not pass) for two reasons: (1) RC2 has three viable resolution options (new adv_* tool vs fold-into-archive-handler vs delete+manual-doc) and the orchestrator must choose the executable-surface direction before planning; (2) agenda items 4-6 (real worker/memory ceiling at 10 sessions) are UNMEASURED — only 4-worker/3.56GB sampled (proposal context) and the ADR-0005 envelope is 'typically <=3 sessions', so the 'supported 5-10 concurrency' claim is unverified, not confirmed-safe. Recommend measurement before release claims a ceiling.

tradeoffs: Routing plugin-init through the helper is the minimal one-owner fix but touches the worker-spawn decision path — the highest blast-radius code in the plugin; needs a test binding the RESOLVED runtime value (not just the helper default) to rq-advcfg01.2.

Exposing a new adv_* tool for trunk sync adds surface area (manifest regeneration, agent policy) but keeps sync explicit and agent-callable; folding into the archive handler adds no surface but couples release finalization to git mutation, narrowing the test boundary that git-finalize.test.ts:4538 currently guards.

Flipping default false multiplies worker processes (1/session). ADR-0005:22 accepts this up to ~3 sessions; at 5-10 it is unmeasured — worker RSS variance (one outlier at 2.03GB in a 4-worker/3.56GB sample) makes linear projection unreliable.
Consolidating the 3 duplicate readBooleanFeatureFlag copies into the helper improves locality/consistency but is wider than the RC1 defect and risks touching worktree-guard paths if done carelessly.

=== CANDIDATE 1: KD2 queue-mode is a conditional at an existing seam, not new routing architecture (SIMPLIFICATION) ===
Candidate: KD2's prose ('Resolve one routing mode at plugin initialization and inject it into Temporal store construction') reads as new architecture, but workflow-start.ts:53-55 ALREADY routes by sessionId presence and changes.ts:659 ALREADY threads getCurrentSessionId(). The entire KD2 runtime change reduces to: store adapter receives workflowQueueMode from plugin-init (which knows the resolved policy) and conditionally omits sessionId from the workflow input when mode==project. Routing falls through to the existing project-queue branch. No ChangeWorkflowInput field, no workflow code change (already C4-compliant). The only genuinely new logic is the INCOMPATIBLE_ACTIVE_SESSION_QUEUES init-time diagnostic.
Evidence: workflow-start.ts:44-55 (existing routing); changes.ts:648-660 (existing sessionId injection); plugin-init.ts:279-289 (policy + plan); 0 existing workflowQueueMode matches (lgrep).
Payoff: high. Bounds implementation estimate; confirms C4 (unchanged workflow contracts) is structurally free, not costly.
Risk: low. sessionId threading is proven; conditional is additive.
Contract tie: AC1, AC10, C4, DDC2.
Prior consideration: new.
Recommended fate: adopt_now.
Fate rationale: Contract-tied, low risk, pure simplification; reduces planning risk by confirming the wiring point pre-exists.

=== CANDIDATE 2: status.ts source-classification loop is a partial ResolvedProjectFeaturePolicy.source map — fold it in (REUSE) ===
Candidate: status.ts:682-687 manually computes featureFlagSources[key] = rawFeatures[key]!==undefined ? 'explicit' : 'default'. KD1's ResolvedProjectFeaturePolicy should own source as explicit|default|invalid_fallback. The existing loop is the resolver's source map minus invalid_fallback. When the resolver owns the source map, status.ts's manual loop (682-687) becomes redundant and should be deleted, consuming the resolver's output instead. This closes a third source of truth and ensures invalid_fallback reaches diagnostics (AC2 currently cannot report invalid_fallback because status.ts never classifies it).
Evidence: status.ts:675-687 (calls resolver then recomputes sources); project.ts:169-183 (canonical resolver, no source classification).
Payoff: medium. Eliminates a third truth owner; adds invalid_fallback to diagnostics for free.
Risk: low. status.ts already calls the resolver; just consume a richer return.
Contract tie: AC2 (explicit/default reporting), AC9 (one effective value across runtime+diagnostics), DDC1.
Prior consideration: new.
Recommended fate: adopt_now.
Fate rationale: Contract-tied, low risk, reduces code surface and closes a classification gap.

=== CANDIDATE 3: Port-registry cleanup lifecycle crosses ADV delete authority and target-repo hooks — leak-detection gap (CROSS-CUTTING RISK) ===
Candidate: KD6 places port/PID namespace reservation 'under the repo external OpenCode project state' with 'pre-delete releases it only after normal ADV deletion safety passes.' But DONT7 forbids weakening worktree cleanup/lease/integration/terminal-proof authority, and OOS2 puts worktree flock/lease/cleanup-authority out of scope. So the port-registry cleanup is a NEW resource lifecycle that must hook the ADV delete path WITHOUT being owned by it. If the target-repo pre-delete hook fails to release a port, the reservation leaks silently — the ADV delete authority (DONT7) has no knowledge of port state. The design's mitigation ('Idempotent lease with PID/session liveness... reclaim only proven stale records') is lazy reclaim on next setup. Under 10 concurrent sessions, a leaked port blocks a new worktree until the next setup's stale-detection fires, amplifying KD4's bounded-lock contention. The design should specify: does a failed port-release hook BLOCK worktree deletion (and thus block fixArchiveCleanupSequencing terminal convergence)? Or is it best-effort with lazy reclaim? This is a user-value tradeoff (reliability vs liveness) the contract does not currently resolve.
Evidence: KD6 ('pre-delete releases it only after normal ADV deletion safety passes'); DONT7; OOS2; DDC7; risk-table line 'Port registry leaks after crash.'
Payoff: high. Prevents a resource leak that only surfaces under the exact 10-agent load target.
Risk: medium. Touches the boundary between ADV delete authority and target-repo hooks; DONT7 constrains cleanup-authority changes.
Contract tie: AC7, DDC7, DONT7.
Prior consideration: new.
Recommended fate: surface_to_user.
Fate rationale: Cross-cutting risk spanning two repos + a DONT constraint; involves a user-value tradeoff (block-on-hook-failure vs lazy-reclaim) that the contract does not resolve — must not auto-adopt.

=== CANDIDATE 4: Both this change and fixArchiveCleanupSequencing restructure archive-gate.ts Phase 9 — define the insertion seam now to avoid rebase collision (SIMPLIFICATION / COORDINATION) ===
Candidate: KD3 inserts syncDefaultBranchAfterMerge into archive-gate.ts Phase 9 (lines 400-434,737). fixArchiveCleanupSequencing ALSO restructures Phase 9 (terminal-convergence helper convergeAndCleanupArchiveSource 'near Phase 9/archive finalization'). Both changes edit the same function. KD3 says 'rebase after fixArchiveCleanupSequencing' but the risk is a code-level collision in the same handler, not just merge ordering. The intended seam is: release-proof-proven -> [KD3 local-sync] -> [fixArchiveCleanupSequencing terminal convergence] -> cleanup. If KD3 defines its insertion as a distinct helper call boundary (not inline edits to the Phase 9 body), fixArchiveCleanupSequencing can land its terminal-convergence helper without conflicting, and KD3's rebase becomes a clean insert-before rather than a line-level merge conflict.
Evidence: archive-gate.ts:400-434 (Phase 9 handler, shared surface); KD3 design ('rebase and inserts local sync'); fixArchiveCleanupSequencing design ('archive-owned helper near Phase 9/archive finalization').
Payoff: medium. Avoids rebase thrash between two active changes touching the same function.
Risk: low. Coordination discipline, not code risk.
Contract tie: C2 (coordinated three-repo), DDC4.
Prior consideration: conflict:fixArchiveCleanupSequencing (explicitly referenced as coordination dependency).
Recommended fate: design_around.
Fate rationale: Contract-tied, low risk, needs design adjustment (extract KD3 local-sync as a helper-call boundary rather than inline Phase 9 edits) to deconflict.

=== CANDIDATE 5: Extract fs.ts acquireFileLock backoff structure as shared primitive for KD4 (REUSE) ===
Candidate: fs.ts:91-166 (acquireFileLock) already implements bounded wall-clock budget + jittered exponential backoff + stale-holder reclaim. KD4 proposes to build the same structure inline at worktree/index.ts:1116-1132 ('exponential delays 25ms base, capped 250ms, bounded jitter, total 1500ms budget'). Two independent implementations of the same retry/backoff pattern will drift in constants and jitter semantics. Extracting the backoff LOOP STRUCTURE (not the file-lock-specific stale-detection, which uses PID/timestamp .lock files vs git-flock) as a shared bounded-acquire-with-backoff primitive lets both call sites share constants and test seams.
Evidence: fs.ts:91-166 (acquireFileLock bounded loop); worktree/index.ts:1116-1132 (one-shot flock, no retry); KD4 ('bounded acquire loop').
Payoff: medium. Reduces new code; prevents drift between two retry loops; KD4's test-seam requirement (injected wait/random/clock) is satisfied for free by the extracted primitive.
Risk: low-medium. acquireFileLock's stale-detection is file-lock-specific (PID/timestamp); git-flock stale reclaim is owned by acquireWorkerLock. Extraction must be scoped to the retry/backoff structure only, not the stale-detection, to avoid coupling file-lock semantics into the flock path.
Contract tie: AC6, DDC5 (lock budget).
Prior consideration: new (design references fs.ts as a 'precedent' but does not propose extraction).
Recommended fate: design_around.
Fate rationale: Contract-tied, low risk, needs design adjustment to scope the shared primitive to backoff structure only.

# Fix multi-session concurrency defaults

## Why

ADV must support ten simultaneous same-project agents across `pokeedge` and `pokeedge-web` without silent workflow stalls, shared-trunk writes, or resource collisions. Current runtime, diagnostics, spec law, and archive instructions disagree about how concurrency works.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Defect origin:** Omitted `worker_singleton_enforce` is reported as `false` but resolved as `true` at worker spawn; peer sessions can therefore lack a poller for their own session queue. Archive prose also instructs the agent to invoke an unexposed TypeScript helper, while both target repos disable trunk-write protection.

**Tier 1 evidence:**

- `withStabilityFeatureDefaults` defaults `worker_singleton_enforce` to `false` (`plugin/src/types/project.ts:169-183`), matching `rq-advcfg01.2`, ADR-0005, deployment notes, and commit `bbbbdbca4`.
- Runtime bypasses that owner and passes hardcoded `true` at `plugin/src/plugin-init.ts:279-283`. `resolveWorkerSingletonPlan` then makes non-owners client-only and skips worker creation (`plugin-init.ts:128-146,300`).
- `syncDefaultBranchAfterMerge` has tests but no production caller or tool wrapper (`git-finalize.ts:189-314`; `git-finalize.test.ts:4538-4565`). `.opencode/command/adv-archive.md:517` cannot call a TypeScript function.
- `pokeedge/project.json` and `pokeedge-web/project.json` explicitly set `worktree_guard_enforce: false`; their default checkouts currently contain 15 and 5 uncommitted paths.

**Tier 2 evidence:** Not applicable; defects are internal and source-verifiable.

**Leading cause:** The May 22 default flip changed the canonical helper, docs, and diagnostics but missed the runtime spawn call site. Later spec reconciliation also restored pre-per-session singleton law, creating code/spec/ADR drift.

**Ruled out:** worktree flock as primary bottleneck; archive fast-forward contention (helper never executes); firewall already protecting target repos.

**Spec-law impact:** `rq-advcfg01.2` contradicts runtime. Current `rq-workerSingleton01` again mandates one worker/project and client-only peers, contradicting ADR-0005 per-session queues and the false default. `rq-temporalConcurrentLoad01` currently specifies only five sessions.

**Inline-RCA rationale:** Audit already traced declaration → loader → runtime decision → effect and disproved alternatives.

## User Outcomes

- Ten simultaneous same-project ADV agents, including orchestrators and sub-agents, remain serviceable.
- Runtime behavior, status diagnostics, docs, and spec law report one consistent worker model.
- Coding work cannot mutate shared trunk checkouts.
- Approved deployment/operations run only from a clean, current default checkout without creating an operations branch or worktree.
- Worktree-local ports, databases, generated state, and dependencies do not interfere across agents.
- Remote/default-branch release proof remains authoritative; failed local sync is loud and non-destructive, not a false release failure.
- Freshness checks prevent decisions based on a trunk snapshot that may be several merges behind.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Canonical feature-default resolution and all duplicate runtime readers
- Runtime-default regression coverage
- Reconciliation of `rq-advcfg01`, `rq-workerSingleton01`, and the ten-session support bar
- Executable post-merge trunk-sync behavior without an internal `git-finalize` caller
- Bounded `BRANCH_LOCKED` contention handling
- Linked `pokeedge` and `pokeedge-web` changes for firewall, worktree resource isolation, and freshness
- Passive/historical evidence and bounded observability for ten-session capacity; no synthetic load test

### Out of Scope

- Temporal workflow contracts or signal shapes
- Rewriting worktree flock, lease, or cleanup authority
- Archive gate/release-proof redesign
- Bulk deletion of existing worktrees/branches
- CI pipeline redesign
- Cross-repo merge-order automation

### Must Not

- Weaken explicit `worker_singleton_enforce: true` compatibility without an approved spec change
- Preserve multiple independent feature-default owners
- Let diagnostics report a value runtime does not use
- Discard existing dirty-trunk work
- Add an internal `git-finalize.ts` call site forbidden by its boundary test
- Poll external state in normal agent context
- Deploy from a worktree or create an operations branch
- Block a remotely proven release solely because local trunk cannot fast-forward safely

## Current State

- Feature resolution has one canonical helper plus three local `readBooleanFeatureFlag*` copies (`plugin-init.ts`, `worktree-auto-manage.ts`, `task.ts`). Only `plugin-init.ts` resolves a wrong value.
- `syncDefaultBranchAfterMerge` is an orphaned executable helper; archive release proof itself is sound.
- Worktree create contention returns `BRANCH_LOCKED` immediately. In-tree bounded retry precedents exist in `utils/fs.ts:91-166` and the DB-init path.
- `pokeedge` has 109 worktrees and 126 local branches; `pokeedge-web` has 41 and 57. Worktree storage totals about 75 GB.
- `pokeedge` worktree setup is empty. `pokeedge-web` shares `node_modules` and documents its install race.
- Over the last 30 days, pokeedge recorded 385 main commits and pokeedge-web 351. Their fastest 10% inter-commit gaps are 233s and 288s; up to four and three commits landed inside five-minute windows. A 300s freshness suppressor can therefore span multiple merges.
- Historical OpenCode data records 12 overlapping pokeedge sessions (6 orchestrators, 6 sub-agents). This proves demand above ten total agents, not ten independent orchestrators. No failed ADV task-queue workflows were observed in the sampled Temporal visibility data.
- Current workers are one per distinct project; the faulty same-project default is latent in the live snapshot, not disproved.

## Skills Considered

- `adv-worktree`: matched; supplied multi-session, cleanup, and merge constraints.
- `adv-arch-detection`: matched; used declaration-versus-runtime and command-surface consistency checks.
- `adv-opportunity-scout`: matched; identified duplicate default readers, stale singleton law, and archived RC2 context.
- No pending-review skill was found; no new skill gap warranted creation.

## Extends

- `temp/temporal-perf-report.md`: prior figures are explicitly synthetic/provisional. New finding: current session DB and Temporal visibility provide real historical concurrency evidence, but not per-session service-latency proof.
- `temp/brainstorm-adv-runtime-enhancements.md`: prior work argued for runtime rather than documentation-only enforcement. New finding: archive Phase 9.5 violates that principle by naming an uncallable helper.
- ADR-0005 and deployment notes: prior work selected per-session queues. New finding: commit `bbbbdbca4` omitted the actual worker-spawn resolver and current spec law later drifted back to singleton MUST semantics.
- Archived `autoDrivePrArchiveCompletion`: previously recorded the trunk-sync invocation gap as a known limitation. New finding: it remains unexecutable and should now be closed.

## Conflict Scan

Inventory completeness: **complete** for 17 active changes plus relevant archived context. Validation passes; `NO_TASKS` and `NO_DELTAS` are expected pre-prep warnings.

- `fixArchiveCleanupSequencing` overlaps archive finalization files and is already through planning. This change must preserve its terminal-convergence ordering and coordinate merge order before changing Phase 9.5.
- `makeToolReadsWorkerFree` is related context but does not own worker-spawn defaults.
- No active change owns feature-default consolidation, target-repo firewall policy, or ten-session support.

## Edge Cases

1. **Feature defaults:** explicit `true` remains honored; `ADV_FORCE_IN_PROCESS_WORKER=1` remains compatible; invalid config fails safely; status/runtime use the same resolved object.
2. **Trunk sync:** wrong branch or dirty trunk receives no mutation; local-ahead divergence remains untouched; fetch/network failure is reported; remote release remains complete.
3. **Worktree lock:** holder exits during wait; holder remains busy beyond bounded budget; concurrent creators for different branches do not duplicate registry entries.
4. **Firewall/operations:** source-changing deploy command is rejected; approved deploy from stale/dirty/non-default trunk is rejected; generated external/gitignored outputs do not authorize arbitrary source writes.
5. **Resource isolation:** existing worktrees remain usable; missing secrets fail setup without copying secrets; shared database operations cannot cross-contaminate test data.

## Related Pattern Scan

- Three private feature-flag readers repeat the same boundary bug class; all are in scope for consolidation.
- No analogous orphaned archive helper was found.
- Bounded retry primitives already exist but are not used for busy worktree flock acquisition.
- `worker_singleton_enforce` is absent from the generated project schema while runtime accepts it through passthrough; discovery classifies schema/spec reconciliation in scope.

## Completeness Verification

**Problem completeness — high confidence.** The audit covered declarations, loaders, worker spawn, status projection, archive control surfaces, worktree contention, target-repo config, historical sessions, worker memory, and freshness data. The issue is broader than one wrong boolean: it includes stale law and unexecutable orchestration.

**Solution-scope completeness — high confidence.** Feature-default readers and archive trunk-sync callers received target-operation scans. No unverified sole-entry claim remains. Secondary surfaces are classified: duplicate readers/spec schema/tests are in scope; workflow contracts, correct status consumers, cleanup authority, and CI are out.

**Reproduction classifications:** missing per-session poller = `broken_capability`; uncallable direct TypeScript invocation = `unwarranted_operation` and must not seed an AC requiring agents to call it; dirty target trunks = `broken_capability` of configured protection, with existing files preserved.

## LBP Check

Purely internal architecture; external tools/libraries are not viable alternatives. Long-term best practice is structural: one typed feature-resolution owner, executable tool/handler boundaries, per-worktree mutable resources, clean/default/current trunk for deployment, and remote canonical release proof. No external-solution search needed.

## Discovery Opportunity Scout

Run: strategic cross-repo architecture change. Five candidates considered. Auto-adopted: consolidate all duplicate feature readers; treat current singleton law as stale; narrow RC2 to executable handler/tool/manual choices. User-surfaced: ten-session evidence timing. Follow-up: stale comment in `worktree-auto-manage.ts` if touched.

## Draft Spec Deltas

### `rq-workerSessionRouting01` — Per-session worker serviceability

- **Given** multiple same-project sessions and default configuration
- **When** each session initializes
- **Then** each session queue has an active poller, while explicit singleton compatibility behavior is separately defined

### `rq-runtimeFeatureDefaults01` — One resolved feature policy

- **Given** a feature is omitted, explicit, or config-invalid
- **When** diagnostics and runtime consume it
- **Then** both observe the same typed resolved value and source classification

### `rq-archiveLocalTrunkSync01` — Non-authoritative local sync

- **Given** remote/default release proof is complete
- **When** local trunk is clean/current/default, diverged, dirty, or unreachable
- **Then** safe fast-forward may run; unsafe cases remain untouched with exact remediation and do not revoke release proof

### `rq-worktreeCreateContention01` — Bounded create contention

- **Given** another process briefly owns the per-project worktree lock
- **When** worktree creation begins
- **Then** acquisition retries within a bounded budget and returns structured `BRANCH_LOCKED` only after exhaustion

### `rq-tenSessionSupport01` — Ten-agent operating envelope

- **Given** historical/current evidence includes at least ten overlapping same-project ADV agents
- **When** capacity and serviceability are assessed without a synthetic load test
- **Then** the report distinguishes observed demand, structural queue coverage, memory budget, and unproven latency; unsupported claims remain explicit

## Recommended Objectives

1. Make runtime, status, docs, and specs agree on one worker-routing policy.
2. Keep ten concurrent same-project agents serviceable within the existing 60 GB / 16-core host budget, using historical/current evidence rather than a synthetic load test.
3. Make archive trunk synchronization executable, safe, and non-authoritative to release proof.
4. Prevent coding writes on target-repo trunks while preserving a narrow, guarded trunk-only deployment path.
5. Isolate mutable worktree resources in both target repos without breaking existing worktrees.
6. Absorb brief worktree-create contention and surface only bounded exhaustion.
7. Reduce freshness exposure from a five-minute window that can contain multiple merges.

## AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS

- **B1 MEDIUM — Boundaries:** coordinated three-repo delivery requires linked per-repo changes and explicit merge order; current change cannot directly own foreign project lifecycle state.
  - Evidence: "Linked `pokeedge` and `pokeedge-web` changes"
  - Resolution: user chose coordinated three-repo outcome; design must define linkage/order.
- **S1 MEDIUM — Completion signals:** historical evidence proves 12 overlapping total agents but only 6 orchestrators; it does not prove ten-session latency.
  - Evidence: "using historical/current evidence rather than a synthetic load test"
  - Resolution: criteria must claim structural serviceability/capacity from observed data, not a synthetic performance result.
- **M1 MEDIUM — Missing information:** exact target-repo port/database/dependency mechanisms remain design questions.
  - Evidence: "Isolate mutable worktree resources"
  - Resolution: defer mechanism to design; behavior is firm.

Coverage: B:P F:C S:P M:P

No CRITICAL or HIGH findings; discovery may proceed to agreement.

# Design — Multi-Session Concurrency

## Architecture Overview

Coordinated outcome, independently tracked in three repos:

```text
Advance: policy → queue routing → archive sync → bounded worktree lock → evidence
   ↓ merged and deployed from fresh trunk
pokeedge: guard + ops gate + backend resources + freshness
pokeedge-web: guard + ops gate + ports/PIDs/dependencies + freshness
```

Advance is source change; target changes carry cross-project origin and keep their own branch, PR, gates, and release proof.

## Key Decisions

### KD1 — One typed feature-policy owner

Create `ResolvedProjectFeaturePolicy` with effective values and source (`explicit | default | invalid_fallback`). `withStabilityFeatureDefaults` becomes/delegates to this owner.

Remove private readers at `plugin-init.ts:161-169`, `worktree-auto-manage.ts:85-93`, `task.ts:292-300`, and status source loop `status.ts:682-687`.

**Levers:** runtime decision `plugin-init.ts:279-300`; status projection `status.ts:675-687`. One omitted/explicit/invalid matrix tests both. Loader validates input; resolver interprets policy. No workflow imports.

### KD2 — Coherent default and explicit-singleton routing

| Policy | Worker | New change queue |
|---|---|---|
| default / false | each session polls own session + project queue | session |
| explicit true | lock owner polls project queue; peers are clients | project |

Existing seam: `workflow-start.ts:53-55` selects queue by `sessionId`; callers at `changes.ts:648-660` and `store-temporal/index.ts:698-709` already inject it. Store receives `workflowQueueMode`; project mode omits `sessionId`. Workflow input/code stay unchanged.

**Worker lever:** `plugin-init.ts:219,275-325` resolves mode and queue list before worker creation.

Explicit singleton refuses activation with `INCOMPATIBLE_ACTIVE_SESSION_QUEUES` while open workflows remain session-pinned. Never silently strand histories. Specs make default per-session routing authoritative and scope `rq-workerSingleton01` to explicit compatibility.

### KD3 — Archive handler executes non-authoritative local sync

After PR `MERGED` proof on idempotent archive re-drive, archive handler invokes `syncDefaultBranchAfterMerge` through a narrow external helper seam, records outcome, then continues existing remote release proof.

**Levers:** `change/archive-gate.ts:403-431,737`; `change.ts`; helper `git-finalize.ts:189-314`.

Add explicit `git status --porcelain` pre-check:

- clean/current/default → fast-forward or already current;
- dirty → `blocked: MAIN_DIRTY`, no mutation;
- diverged → bounded local-only commits, no mutation;
- fetch/wrong-branch/TOCTOU failure → exact remediation, no destructive retry.

Non-synced local outcomes remain warnings after canonical remote proof—not release failures. No general sync tool; no internal `git-finalize.ts` caller. Remove prose asking model to call TypeScript.

`fixArchiveCleanupSequencing` lands first. This inserts one seam before its terminal-convergence/cleanup boundary and preserves proof → terminal readback → worktree removal → branch deletion.

### KD4 — Bounded worktree lock acquisition

Keep `git-worktree.lock` as sole git filesystem coordination. Reuse/extract only the generic backoff loop shape from `utils/fs.ts:91-166`; stale-holder semantics remain in `acquireWorkerLock`.

At `worktree/index.ts:1116-1132`: 1,500 ms wall budget, 25 ms exponential base, 250 ms cap, bounded jitter. Exhaustion returns existing `BRANCH_LOCKED` plus attempts/elapsed. Lock never spans setup hooks. Tests inject wait/random/clock and prove one registration/path.

### KD5 — Trunk guard plus repo operations gate

After preserving/relocating current trunk dirt, set `worktree_guard_enforce:true` in both target repos.

No firewall bypass. Because script-internal writes are intentionally outside firewall parsing (`trunk-write-firewall.ts:383-398`), every local production/rebuild/install/release entrypoint composes repo-owned `bin/trunk-ops-gate`.

Gate proves: main non-linked checkout; resolved default; clean status except exact operation-owned generated paths; fresh/zero-behind; operation in static enum and script mapping. Unknown/error refuses. CI fresh checkouts are separate. No operations worktree or deployment branch.

### KD6 — Stable worktree resource identity

Each target repo has one idempotent setup script deriving identity from git common-dir + branch and writing gitignored `.opencode/worktree.env`; secrets never copied.

A short shared registry lock allocates collision-checked port blocks/namespaces. Re-run reuses reservation; hash-only allocation is not authority.

**Port-reservation cleanup choice:** recommended policy is nonblocking release. Pre-delete attempts release but failure does not block ADV deletion. Reservation has process/session liveness plus lease expiry; next setup reclaims only proven-stale records. Alternative is blocking deletion until release succeeds, which prevents temporary leaks but can stall archive on auxiliary state.

#### pokeedge

- worktree-local `.venv` with shared uv download cache;
- reserved API/frontend ports;
- per-worktree test DB/schema and Redis namespace; provider budgets stay global;
- DB preflight/flock retained;
- template-only worktree setup hooks, never `.env`;
- hardcoded Vision/MCP cwd explicitly out of scope as separate tool-routing capability.

#### pokeedge-web

- `symlinkDirs: []`; isolated `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, then existing prepare/Svelte sync;
- reserved frontend/backend/Playwright ports; fixed CI overrides allowed;
- PID/log paths under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pokeedge-dev/<worktree-id>/`;
- remove cross-worktree process kill; stop only recorded current-worktree PIDs;
- preserve existing local generated/cache paths.

Existing worktrees are never rewritten automatically. New creation uses settings; resume offers idempotent migration without deleting/replacing files.

### KD7 — Trigger-driven ≤60s freshness

Both target repos track `bin/oc-fresh-project`, exporting `OC_FRESH_TTL=60` and delegating to host `oc-fresh`. Instructions route before-judgment, pre-push/PR, and post-wait checks through it. Shared git-common-dir marker remains. No timer/daemon/polling.

### KD8 — Passive ten-agent evidence

Advance adds a bounded read-only collector over existing OpenCode session DBs, Temporal visibility, process metadata, and workload-gate events. It launches no sessions/workflows.

It reports population-consistent overlap split by orchestrator/sub-agent, queues/failures, RSS/host budget, worktree storage, test wait, window/provenance, and limits.

Baseline: 12 total overlapping pokeedge agents, 6 orchestrators; zero failed sampled ADV queue workflows; worker RSS 314 MB–2.03 GB. May establish ten total-agent demand/observation; must not claim ten-orchestrator latency.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Merge `fixArchiveCleanupSequencing`; rebase.
2. Advance: policy/source map and routing conditional.
3. Advance: singleton incompatibility diagnostic, specs/docs/tests.
4. Advance: archive sync seam + `MAIN_DIRTY` pre-check + command cleanup.
5. Advance: bounded lock acquisition + evidence collector.
6. Verify/build/merge; deploy only from fresh merged Advance trunk; restart plugin host.
7. Create linked pokeedge and pokeedge-web changes.
8. Preserve/relocate trunk dirt; enable guard; add ops gates.
9. Add resource setup and freshness wrappers; migrate only new/resumed worktrees.
10. Merge target changes independently after repo-specific acceptance.

## LBP Analysis

Structural owners: one policy, existing routing seam, executable archive handler, bounded lock loop, collision-detecting resource registry, canonical-source operations gate, event-triggered freshness.

Rejected: one-line boolean patch; general git-sync tool; local-sync release blocking; operations worktree; mutable dependency symlinks; hash-only ports; synthetic load test; auxiliary port cleanup as archive authority.

## Design-Derived Criteria

1. **DDC1:** one production feature-policy resolver/source classifier.
2. **DDC2:** default uses session queue/per-session worker; explicit singleton uses project queue and refuses incompatible pinned queues.
3. **DDC3:** all Worker creation paths retain tuning caps.
4. **DDC4:** local sync never checkout/switch/pull/reset/force or mutate dirty/diverged trunk; cannot authorize release.
5. **DDC5:** lock acquire returns within 1.5s plus one git invocation; no real test sleeps.
6. **DDC6:** unknown op, dirty/non-default/linked/stale checkout, or probe error blocks local production mutation.
7. **DDC7:** ten live reservations cannot share port/namespace; setup idempotent; secrets uncopied; auxiliary release never weakens ADV deletion.
8. **DDC8:** existing worktrees not automatically rewritten/deleted.
9. **DDC9:** target wrappers set TTL ≤60s and preserve host failures.
10. **DDC10:** evidence is read-only, bounded, population-consistent, and separates total agents from orchestrators.

## Risks / Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Spec drift | canonical generation + cross-asset assertions |
| Session-pinned histories | detect/refuse singleton switch |
| Archive edit collision | cleanup change first + narrow seam + rebase |
| Worker memory variance | retain caps + explicit evidence limits |
| Port release crash | nonblocking lease expiry + proven-stale reclaim |
| Ops gate false block | exact enum + actionable reason; no blanket disable |
| Dirty trunks | inspect/relocate before flip |
| External service contamination | per-worktree DB/schema/Redis; global budgets global |
| Dependency cost | package-manager caches, not mutable symlinks |
| Freshness wrapper bypass | repo instruction/test routing; host force fallback |

## ADR Drafts

Amend ADR-0005 with corrected runtime default, conditional singleton mode, ten-agent evidence boundary, and pinned-session refusal.

## Design Leverage Scout

Five candidates considered. Auto-adopted existing routing seam and policy-owned status source map. Designed around archive helper seam and reusable backoff loop. Surfaced for approval: nonblocking lease-based port cleanup versus making auxiliary cleanup block worktree deletion.
